topic.title: Review Task States and Status
topic.shortdesc: This topic explains the states a review task can have and how those states are shown to owners and reviewers.

body.p: The states of a review task depend on the type of review task because project review tasks and independent review tasks have different workflows. Task owners move a task from one state to another. The review status is how the task state is shown to a user based on the user's review task role. For owners, the review status matches the task state. For reviewers, the review status shows only the states that are relevant to that role.

section.title: Review status versus review task state
section.p: The review status depends on both the task state and the role of the collaborator. In most cases, the review status matches the task state. In some cases, a later task state is not relevant to reviewers, so reviewers see the status Review closed instead of the actual task state. For example, a sees Review closed for a task that is in the Review closed state or in later states that are not relevant to reviewers.

section.title: Project Review Task States
section.p: A Project Review Task can be in one of the following states: In review, Review closed, Integrating, or Integrated.
The following table shows how each task state is presented as review status:

table.title: How task state is rendered as review status based on the role

section.p: The following list describes each state:

li.p: In review - This is the initial state for newly created review tasks. Tasks remain in this state until a task owner closes the review. Both reviewers and task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. To close the review a task owner can use the Close review button, and the task will transition to the Review closed state.

Review closed - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Close review button. Only task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. The files are read-only for reviewers. Task owners can reopen the task using the Reopen review button, and its state returns to In review or they can start the integration process to merge the task changes into the original content using the Start integration button. Only one owner will be able to use the Start integration action to keep the integration responsibility with a single person.

Integrating - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Start integration button to integrate the task changes into the project. Only the task owner who started the integration can edit the task files while the task is in this state. The files are read-only for all other collaborators. From this state the owner that handles the integration can use Cancel integration to return to the Review closed state, or finalize the integration and merge the changes into the original project content using the Finish integration button.

Integrated - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Finish integration button after the integration is complete. Task files are read-only for all participants. An integrated review task can no longer be reopened.

section.note: The review status presented to reviewers for the Integrating and Integrated states is Review closed because, from the reviewer's point of view, these states are equivalent to the Review closed state.

section.title: Independent Review Task States
section.p: An Independent Review Task can be in one of the following states: In review, Review closed, or Integrated.

table.title: How task state is rendered as review status based on the role

li.p: In review - This is the initial state for newly created review tasks. Tasks remain in this state until a task owner closes the review. Both reviewers and task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. To close the review a task owner can use the Close review button, and the task will transition to the Review closed state.

Review closed - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Close review button. Only task owners can edit the task files while the task is in this state. The files are read-only for reviewers. Task owners can reopen the task using the Reopen review button, and its state returns to In review, or they can mark that they integrated the content of the task using the Mark as integrated button, and the task will transition to the Integrated state.

Integrated - Tasks change to this state when a task owner uses the Mark as integrated button on a closed task to mark that the content of the task was integrated and it is not needed anymore. In this state, task files are read-only for all participants and the task is visible only to the task owners. Using the Mark as not integrated button allows owners to transition the task back to the Review closed state.
